label: Person
name: Publius Cornelius Lentulus
summary:
Publius Cornelius Lentulus was a Roman politician and general who played a pivotal role in shaping the late Republic.

Born into a prominent family, Lentulus rose through the ranks of Roman politics, collaborating with Julius Caesar and Pompey to dominate the Senate. His military campaigns in Gaul expanded Rome's territories, but his defeat at Pharsalus led to his downfall.

Despite this, Lentulus's legacy endured through his influence on the development of Roman law and governance, leaving a lasting impact on Western legal systems.

As he navigated the treacherous landscape of Roman politics, Lentulus's actions had far-reaching consequences, including the rise of Caesarism and the transformation of the Roman Republic into the Empire.

One oft-quoted phrase encapsulates Lentulus's enduring influence: 'The law is a body of rules which are made by society to govern its own affairs.' - Polybius, Histories (Book VI, Chapter 11).
